scope: Two exact early-main formal-group source applications; no new proof source or ordinary consumer node.

available_assertion.statement: The integral Weierstrass formal chart gives a formal group; its logarithm is additive on the maximal ideal and an isomorphism on depth r>v(p)/(p-1).
available_assertion.objects: An integral Weierstrass equation and its formal group over a complete characteristic-zero DVR.
available_assertion.hypotheses: v(K*)=Z; integral coefficients; residue characteristic p; for the isomorphism, integral r>v(p)/(p-1).
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every such equation, field, and permitted r.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Only the indicated formal subgroup; no assertion on arbitrary elliptic points.
available_assertion.uniformity: Exact algebraic and local statements; no varying-curve analytic uniformity.
available_assertion.constants: The threshold is v(p)/(p-1); first logarithm coefficient is1.
available_assertion.normalizations: z=-x/y; w=-1/y; formal chart x=z/w(z), y=-1/w(z); integer-normalized valuation.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The integral formal chart does not require minimality. The separate E1 identification from VII.2.2 does. Identity is z=0.
available_assertion.limit_order: Construct the integral formal group, then evaluate convergent series and restrict to the indicated depth.

rows.needed: For the displayed integral equation, w=1/x has valuation twice that of z=-x/y; the logarithm is additive and isometric on depth v(z)>e/(p-1), giving v(z([n]Q))=v(z(Q))+v(n) for nonzero integer n and nonzero Q in that depth.
rows.derivation: The source auxiliary coordinate is -1/y, whereas this paragraph uses w=1/x. Its integral Laurent chart gives 1/x=z^2 times an integral unit. Integrating the integral invariant differential gives degree-r logarithm coefficient with denominator dividing r. If v(z)>e/(p-1), (r-1)v(z)-e*v_p(r)>0 for r>=2, so logarithm has leading valuation v(z). Multiplication preserves this depth for integer n; additivity and injectivity yield the displayed valuation identity.
rows.boundary: Completeness, integral coefficients, integer-normalized valuation, formal membership and the strict depth inequality are required. No isometry at the boundary or outside the formal subgroup; n=0 and Q=O are excluded from the valuation identity.

available_assertion.statement: For a minimal integral model, reduction has exact kernel E1 in E0, and the formal group on the maximal ideal identifies with E1.
available_assertion.objects: An elliptic curve over a complete discretely valued field, its minimal model and nonsingular special-fibre group.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Minimal integral Weierstrass equation and completeness. Points consumed by reduction lie in E0.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every such field/model; every point of E0.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Nonsingular reduction subgroup, not all integral points without checking nonsingularity.
available_assertion.uniformity: Exact group maps, with no quantitative estimate.
available_assertion.normalizations: Reduction kernel E1, formal parameter z=-x/y; integral minimal coordinates.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Singular reductions require checking the point is nonsingular. Identity maps to identity.
available_assertion.limit_order: Check the minimal model and E0 membership before taking the finite reduction order.

rows.needed: When the displayed equation is a minimal integral model, identify its formal group with the kernel of nonsingular reduction.
rows.derivation: Apply VII.2.1–2.2 only to the minimal model explicitly stipulated here. The exact reduction sequence identifies the formal subgroup with E1 inside E0; it is not an identification of all integral points.
rows.boundary: Minimality and nonsingular reduction membership remain explicit conditions. No minimality of an arbitrary integral equation is inferred.
